Environment::Environment(IsolateData* isolate_data,
                         Isolate* isolate,
                         const std::vector<std::string>& args,
                         const std::vector<std::string>& exec_args,
                         const EnvSerializeInfo* env_info,
                         EnvironmentFlags::Flags flags,
                         ThreadId thread_id,
                         std::string_view thread_name)
    : isolate_(isolate),
      external_memory_accounter_(new ExternalMemoryAccounter()),
      isolate_data_(isolate_data),
      async_hooks_(isolate, MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, async_hooks)),
      immediate_info_(isolate, MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, immediate_info)),
      timeout_info_(isolate_, 1, MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, timeout_info)),
      tick_info_(isolate, MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, tick_info)),
      timer_base_(uv_now(isolate_data->event_loop())),
      exec_argv_(exec_args),
      argv_(args),
      exec_path_(Environment::GetExecPath(args)),
      exit_info_(
          isolate_, kExitInfoFieldCount, MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, exit_info)),
      should_abort_on_uncaught_toggle_(
          isolate_,
          1,
          MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, should_abort_on_uncaught_toggle)),
      stream_base_state_(isolate_,
                         StreamBase::kNumStreamBaseStateFields,
                         MAYBE_FIELD_PTR(env_info, stream_base_state)),
      time_origin_(performance::performance_process_start),
      time_origin_timestamp_(performance::performance_process_start_timestamp),
      environment_start_(PERFORMANCE_NOW()),
      flags_(flags),
      thread_id_(thread_id.id == static_cast<uint64_t>(-1)
                     ? AllocateEnvironmentThreadId().id
                     : thread_id.id),

static Local<ArrayBuffer> New(
      Isolate* isolate, size_t byte_length,
      BackingStoreInitializationMode initialization_mode =
          BackingStoreInitializationMode::kZeroInitialized);

  /**
   * Create a new ArrayBuffer with an existing backing store.
   * The created array keeps a reference to the backing store until the array
   * is garbage collected. Note that the IsExternal bit does not affect this
   * reference from the array to the backing store.
   *
   * In future IsExternal bit will be removed. Until then the bit is set as
   * follows. If the backing store does not own the underlying buffer, then
   * the array is created in externalized state. Otherwise, the array is created
   * in internalized state. In the latter case the array can be transitioned
   * to the externalized state using Externalize(backing_store).
   */
  static Local<ArrayBuffer> New(Isolate* isolate,
                                std::shared_ptr<BackingStore> backing_store);

  /**
   * Returns a new standalone BackingStore that is allocated using the array
   * buffer allocator of the isolate. The allocation can either be zero
   * initialized, or uninitialized. The result can be later passed to
   * ArrayBuffer::New.
   *
   * If the allocator returns nullptr, then the function may cause GCs in the
   * given isolate and re-try the allocation.
   *
   * If GCs do not help and on_failure is kOutOfMemory, then the
   * function will crash with an out-of-memory error.
   *
   * Otherwise if GCs do not help (or the allocation is too large for GCs to
   * help) and on_failure is kReturnNull, then a null result is returned.
   */
  static std::unique_ptr<BackingStore> NewBackingStore(
      Isolate* isolate, size_t byte_length,
      BackingStoreInitializationMode initialization_mode =
          BackingStoreInitializationMode::kZeroInitialized,
      BackingStoreOnFailureMode on_failure =
          BackingStoreOnFailureMode::kOutOfMemory);

actual_order: Environment constructs one actual AliasedInt32Array with four entries. Native field reads/writes address that same storage.

allocate_managed_buffer first creates an uninitialized standalone BackingStore, then builds uv_buf_t from its actual Data/ByteLength, then emplaces the unique owner in the native pointer-key unordered_map.

release_managed_buffer returns an empty unique owner for null base. Otherwise it checks membership, moves the exact owner out, then erases that native map node. It does not allocate or manufacture a JS ArrayBuffer.
OnStreamRead establishes HandleScope/Context before releasing the map entry. nread zero returns; negative calls onread with an empty ArrayBuffer Local and then destroys any local backing.

Positive short read retains old_bs while allocating a new uninitialized exact-length store and copying nread bytes. old_bs is destroyed at the end of that if-block before the ArrayBuffer wrapper is created.

ArrayBuffer::New consumes the native owner only at the later wrapper stage. CallJSOnreadMethod writes read_bytes_or_error then array_buffer_offset, selects the actual internal onread function, then calls the real AsyncWrap MakeCallback.

Environment destructor body completes before native members retire. The map is declared after stream_base_state, which is after async/tick members; map retirement must precede the stream alias and earlier alias owners.
Selected FileHandle ReadStart returns before allocation for zero length; otherwise its suggested extent is at most 65536.
abi_requirements: Create a distinct fixed, non-shared, whole native BackingStore entitlement without allocating a JS wrapper or invoking a guest constructor/getter.
Preserve the uninitialized allocation mode. No additional zero fill is required for this selected Source path; only the actual read/copy extent becomes exposed.
An empty store has logical byte_length zero and Data null in the original BackingStore::Allocate. Do not conflate a zero-length whole store with a missing owner.

Native allocation uses the installed original memory/storage provider and retains its native owner independently of Engine/Context/JS wrapper lifetime. Native duplicate/release operations clear the owned token before destruction and do not require a live VM.

The later intrinsic ArrayBuffer adoption consumes the actual whole native owner on all outcomes. It must not copy the bytes or allocate an earlier wrapper. Its failure/partial-adoption cleanup must release exactly the consumed entitlement.
Adoption must not accept an arbitrary view subspan or unmanaged external buffer as a whole managed store. Do not silently use the existing throwing view-acquisition path.
Preserve existing JS-created ArrayBuffer zero initialization, RAB/GSAB rules and throwing view lease behavior. The new bridge is additive.

Backing allocation failure is the original default kOutOfMemory path at the literal site v8::ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore. It is distinct from the CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST heap-intrinsic owner; exact native fatal details and retry mapping remain a separate explicit seam.
The native map preserves original std::unordered_map operations/iteration and uses the shared real standard-container allocator domain. A pointer-key lookup itself needs no copied string key.

An empty out-of-line map must not introduce a new allocation cutpoint. Proposed placement is aligned tail storage in the existing one native Environment allocation, with runtime native sizeof/alignment accessors and exact combined charge/retirement extent.
VM owns final backing C/H API names, implementation and controls. Modules owns the shared standard allocator/new_handler policy. SDK owns the StreamBase/store/Environment composition and controls.
